function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since antiquity.  The modern scientific study of electricity began in the 16th‑17th centuries with figures such as:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | First recorded observations of static electricity (rubber rubbed with fur). |
| **William Gilbert** (1544‑1603) | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coining the term “electricity.” |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (1706‑1790) | Conducted kite‑experiment, proved electricity is a single fluid, introduced positive/negative charges. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1745‑1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (first battery) in 1800, providing a steady electric current. |
| **André-Marie Ampère** (1775‑1836) | Formulated Ampère’s law, linking current to magnetic fields. |
| **Michael Faraday** (1791‑1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction (Faraday’s law). |
| **James Clerk Maxwell** (1831‑1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations. |

So while no single “discoverer” exists, the foundational work of these scientists—and many others—laid the groundwork for our modern understanding of electricity.
